profile.summary: JESTR (Joint Embedding Space Technique for Ranking) annotates metabolites from tandem mass spectra. It embeds a query MS/MS spectrum and each candidate molecule into one shared space and ranks the candidates by cosine similarity, without predicting a fingerprint or simulating a spectrum. The candidates are typically molecules from PubChem with the right mass or formula.

summary_quotes.text: JESTR leverages the insight that molecules and their corresponding spectra are views of the same data and effectively embeds their representations in a joint space.
Candidate structures are ranked based on cosine similarity between the embeddings of query spectrum and each candidate.
Each entry is a list of candidates for that molecule downloaded from PubChem.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: The molecule encoder is a graph convolutional network over atom and bond features, followed by max pooling and two fully connected layers. The spectrum is binned into 1 Da bins up to 1000 Da (peaks above are dropped), intensities are normalised and log-transformed, and the 1000-dimension vector is passed through a three-layer MLP. The two encoders are trained with a contrastive InfoNCE loss so that a spectrum and its molecule are close. Late in training the model is regularised with candidate molecules that share a formula with training molecules, which the authors report improves rank@1.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The repository releases pretrained weights for two training sets, each as three files: a molecule encoder, a spectrum encoder and a third model file named pretrained_inter_model: NPLIB1 (run id 1707829192911) and MassSpecGym (run id 1741546103623). The NPLIB1 data is included, with large files on Zenodo; NIST and other licensed datasets used in the paper are not released. The released weights are for GPU-trained models. A result should name the weight set (NPLIB1 or MassSpecGym) and whether candidate regularisation was used.

sections.title: Use in benchmarks
sections.body: The MSAlign benchmark paper (an existing source on this record) ran JESTR as a retrieval baseline and describes it as a simple contrastive model pretrained with batch InfoNCE and fine-tuned with the more expensive candidate InfoNCE.

quotes.text: JESTR [33] is a simple contrastive model that pretrains with batch InfoNCE (4) and finetunes with the more computationally expensive candidates InfoNCE (6).

strengths.text: Simple design: two small encoders and cosine ranking, with no fingerprint prediction or spectrum simulation.

quotes.text: Unlike prior approaches that “explicitly” construct molecular FPs or spectra

strengths.text: The authors report that JESTR outperformed other tools by 55.5% to 302.6% on average for rank@1 to rank@20 across four datasets (the authors' claim).

quotes.text: On average, for rank@[1–20], JESTR outperforms other tools by 55.5%–302.6%.
